Keysight Technologies reported revenue of 1846000000.00 and net income of 397000000.00 for the quarter ended 2026-07-31, with a gross margin of 0.658722 and a net margin of 0.215060 [D1]. The stock closed at 333.42, trading above its 20-day simple moving average of 330.4675 and below immediate resistance edges at 366.41, while facing support at 332.78 with a strength rating of 59 [D1]. Management raised its outlook for the fourth quarter to a revenue range of 1930000000.00 to 1950000000.00 and non-GAAP earnings per share between 3.34 and 3.40, citing strong demand in AI infrastructure and commercial communications [D1]. The company expects fiscal year 2026 revenue growth of 32% and EPS growth of approximately 60% at the midpoint based on a weighted diluted share count of approximately 172 million shares [D3].

The market is arguing about whether supply constraints will limit near-term revenue conversion despite robust order growth, with management noting that the supply environment is less flexible than a year ago and acts as a governor on ability to convert demand into revenue [D3]. Analysts have set a mean price target of 418.42, indicating potential upside from current levels, though some caution that price targets may be overly optimistic due to business incentives [D7]. The consensus view suggests strong agreement among analysts regarding the company's ability to report better earnings than predicted earlier, which strengthens the case for near-term stock price movement [D7]. Investors are also weighing the sustainability of $2 billion quarterly order levels and whether supply chain limitations will cause revenue conversion to be nonlinear over the next several quarters [D4].

The plan therefore involves maintaining a bullish stance supported by expanding margins and robust cash generation, with free cash flow reaching 403000000.00 and shareholders equity at 6571000000.00 [D2]. Management intends to continue returning capital through its share repurchase programme while working with suppliers to deconstrain the supply chain for high-demand new product introductions [D4]. The company expects to realize 80% to 90% of the 100000000.00 in cost synergies on a run-rate basis exiting the fiscal year, further supporting its financial flexibility and long-term value creation strategy [D3].
